clue.text: Extra dishes will offer this bit of salad

indicators.note: the two words will offer up a run of letters lying across their join

explanation.surface: A diner is told that ordering extra side dishes will bring a garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will offer' points to the run spanning the end of 'Extra' and the start of 'dishes'.
explanation.definitionFit: This red root vegetable is a familiar sliced ingredient in a green salad.

clue.text: Bit of circuitry deteriorates and is to be pulled up — engineers to the fore!

indicators.note: to the fore puts the engineers at the front of the answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: in a down clue being pulled up reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: rots means deteriorates
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faulty part in a circuit board must be removed, so the engineers step forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be pulled up' reads ROTSIS upwards, giving SISTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistor is a component that opposes current in an electrical circuit.

clue.text: Of the French learners sitting on a road one is not very bright

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: du is French for of the
L is a learner driver's plate, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: French learner drivers on a road are not exactly bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted, dim person.

clue.text: Trader about to set up south of Paddington, say?

indicators.note: in a down clue south of places the second piece below the first

parts.note: Paddington is a London railway station

indicators.note: in a down clue set up reads the word upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A merchant is about to set up shop somewhere below Paddington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RE into ER. Paddington is a London terminus, not the bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper and writing materials.

clue.text: Europeans only half like a saint surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order
only the front half of the word like is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that people from a continent are only half as saintly as one might think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps LI from 'like'; 'surprisingly' rearranges LI with A SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Italy are natives of a European country, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: Perpetual student may be proceeding thus as much as possible

definitions.text: Perpetual student may be proceeding thus
definitions.meaning: an endless student keeps taking one degree after another, an nth one

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to the utmost extent, and literally a student working toward yet another qualification.

clue.text: Prisoner — one going down for strangling female?

indicators.note: strangling means the outer piece grips the inner one

parts.note: a lier is one who lies down

explanation.surface: A convict is sent down for throttling a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going down' mimics being sent to prison; here a lier is simply someone lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a convict serving a life sentence.

clue.text: Like beginning of the journey on a horse perhaps

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: beginning of keeps only the first letter of the word the

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Setting off on a trip on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits astride a horse, one leg on each side.

clue.text: Fodder is served up with endless drink

indicators.note: in a down clue served up reads the little word upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless drops the last letter of the drink

parts.note: lager is a drink

explanation.surface: Animal feed is dished out along with a never-ending drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns IS into SI; 'endless' cuts LAGER to LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is fermented grass stored as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Joint operation of obeisance

parts.note: flexing the knee joint is a gesture of submission

explanation.surface: A coordinated act of homage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint operation' suggests teamwork; it is the action of a body joint, the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling is the act of deference, and also literally flexing a joint.

clue.text: Fish provided by a chap, the only supplier

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
a gent is a chap, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A fishmonger boasts that a fellow is the only one who can provide it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole agent is the exclusive distributor of a product in an area.

clue.text: Corpulent American gangster causing death

parts.note: corpulent means fat
Al Capone, the Chicago mobster, is the gangster Al of crosswords

explanation.surface: A plump US mobster is responsible for a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal or deadly is described as fatal.

clue.text: Bread is thrown out for e.g. gull

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a loaf away to feed a gull on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is an example of a bird of the sea coast.

clue.text: Maybe listener's one hanging on

parts.note: the listener is an ear, and the piece of jewellery hanging on it is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone patiently stays on the line waiting to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging on' suggests a telephone caller holding; it is a jewel dangling from the ear, the listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear jewellery dangles from the lobe, the organ a listener uses.

clue.text: Ancient Edmund, behold, making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means both pieces return, read from back to front

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edmund
lo is an old word for behold

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Edmund stages a return to the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is a literary adjective for times long past, synonymous with ancient.

clue.text: People eating informally may have such famous people

definitions.text: People eating informally may have such
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a casual buffet means there are ...

explanation.definitionFit: Notables are distinguished people, and a casual meal standing up has no tables.

clue.text: Farm animal, sleepy type in tractor

parts.note: a bull is a farm animal
a dozer is someone who dozes

explanation.surface: A bull and a drowsy farmhand are found in a farm vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldozer is a heavy tracked tractor with a front blade.

clue.text: Possibly an anorexic quality seen in a queen wearing not so much

indicators.note: wearing means the outer word is put on around the inner

parts.note: less means not so much
Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A thin queen dressed in skimpy clothing shows a worrying slimness.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinness, lack of fat, could be a trait of someone with anorexia.

clue.text: Worked in musical show with Irish father on TV?

parts.note: an opera is a sung stage show
Father Ted is a television sitcom about an Irish priest

explanation.surface: Someone had a job in a stage musical alongside a priest from a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted was a 1990s Channel 4 sitcom about a hapless priest on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Operated means functioned or ran, as a machine that worked.

clue.text: One's answer here will be criticised

definitions.text: One's answer here will be criticised

parts.words: One's answer here will be criticised
parts.note: what is entered here is literally written in the down light, and the phrase means disparaged

explanation.surface: A student fears the response given will be attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is written into a down light, so it is literally put down, which also means criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down someone is to belittle them; here an entry is set in a down light.

clue.text: Philosopher sounding secure

indicators.note: sounding means the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to lock is to secure

explanation.surface: A thinker who seems to be safe and sound.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: Result of naval economies? It's a bit hairy!

definitions.text: Result of naval economies? It's a bit hairy!

parts.words: Result of naval economies? It's a bit hairy!
parts.note: cutting a ship's crew would be a naval saving, and the phrase is also a short haircut

explanation.surface: Navy budget cuts lead to a risky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit hairy' seems to mean risky; it describes a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short cropped hairstyle, here punningly a reduction in sailors.

clue.text: Copy a component of the periodic table

definitions.meaning: a duplicate made with transfer paper

definitions.text: a component of the periodic table
definitions.meaning: a chemical element, atomic number six

explanation.definitionFit: Element number six, and a duplicate document made with carbon paper.

clue.text: Performer taking part is terrific? Not entirely

indicators.note: taking signals that letters are drawn out of the following words
not entirely shows only some of the letters of those words are used

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stage player's role is wonderful, and gets a lukewarm answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'Not entirely' point to the run inside 'part is terrific'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Fish was out-of-date seemingly

definitions.meaning: food past its date gave off a bad odour, a British past tense of smell

explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery fish, and the British past tense of a verb for giving off an odour.

clue.text: Regret having to abandon river — no flipping fish!

indicators.note: to abandon shows a letter leaves the word for regret

parts.note: a grudge here is resentful regret

indicators.note: flipping shows the little word no is turned over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler laments leaving the river with not a single fish caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' drops R from GRUDGE, giving GUDGE; 'flipping' turns NO into ON. 'flipping' also reads as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The gudgeon is a small European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Drink brings audible sounds of disapproval

indicators.note: audible means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: boos are jeers of disapproval

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking draws jeers from onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Starts to think zanily, being into crazy Chinese philosopher

indicators.note: being into means those letters are set inside the rest
crazy suggests the word Chinese is jumbled
starts to picks out the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A wild-minded thinker from China starts musing eccentrically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' looks like a description of the philosopher, but it signals the shuffle of the word Chinese, which then holds the two opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was the nineteenth-century German thinker of the will to power.

clue.text: Put down at this number!

parts.note: the entry reading put down sits at the down clue with this number in the grid

explanation.surface: An instruction to note something at a particular figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer PUT DOWN appears at 19 down, so the number at which it is entered is the answer here.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid number of the down light whose answer is the phrase put down.

clue.text: Deserter captured by American soldiers gets free

indicators.note: captured by means the deserter goes inside the soldiers

parts.note: GIs are US army soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A runaway is caught by US troops and then released.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without charge, meaning free.
